gloss: to relate; to associate; to connect

definitions.gloss: to relate; to associate; to connect (one thing with another)
definitions.explanation: To draw or establish a logical connection between two or more things, especially when analyzing, explaining, or thinking critically about how they are related.

examples.japanese: この{事件|じけん}を{過去|かこ}の{事例|じれい}と{関連|かんれん}づけた。
examples.english: I connected this incident with past cases.

examples.japanese: {理論|りろん}と{実践|じっせん}を{関連|かんれん}づけて{考|かんが}える。
examples.english: Think by connecting theory and practice.

examples.japanese: {歴史的|れきしてき}な{背景|はいけい}と{関連|かんれん}づけて{説明|せつめい}してください。
examples.english: Please explain it in relation to its historical background.

notes:
Formed from {関連|かんれん} (relation, connection) and the verb-forming suffix づける. Used when drawing connections or establishing relationships between separate things, especially in analytical, academic, or explanatory contexts.

USAGE:
The pattern is: AをBと{関連|かんれん}づける (to connect A with B). Can also use に instead of と.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- 〜と{関連|かんれん}づける: to relate to ~
- 〜に{関連|かんれん}づけて{考|かんが}える: to think in connection with ~
- {知識|ちしき}を{関連|かんれん}づける: to connect pieces of knowledge
- {原因|げんいん}と{関連|かんれん}づける: to connect with a cause

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {結|むす}びつける: to tie together, to link — more concrete, emphasizes binding
- {関連|かんれん}する: to be related — intransitive, describes an existing connection
- {関係|かんけい}づける: to relate — very similar, sometimes interchangeable
